speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if you have any history of smoking or recent infections?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning weight loss combined with your symptoms. Have you noticed any changes in your bowel movements, such as blood in the stool or a change in stool frequency? Also, do you have any history of blood disorders or unexplained bruising?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), abdominal pain, and a painless, fixed supraclavicular mass is highly suggestive of lymphoma, likely involving the retroperitoneum and draining nodes. I recommend immediate staging with a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, followed by a lymph node biopsy. REQUEST TEST: CBC, LDH, ESR. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Chest_Abdomenum_Pelvis.
